before.known: do you have time to practise speaking with you this evening
before.target: an bhfuil am agat labhairt a chleachtadh leat anocht

problem: R8/meaning: 'practise speaking with you' makes no sense after 'do you have time' addressed to the same 'you'.
evidence: Known asks 'do you have time to practise speaking with you', which is reflexive nonsense in English.

before.known: we need to make sure we practise speaking with you as often as we can
before.target: caithfidh muid a chinntiú go mbeidh muid ag labhairt a chleachtadh leat chomh minic agus is féidir linn

problem: Grammar: 'go mbeidh muid ag labhairt a chleachtadh' is ungrammatical and does not match the known 'we practise'.
evidence: The Irish future progressive is combined with a verbal noun phrase, which is not valid; the known has no future progressive.

before.known: I enjoy practising speaking with you more and more and I can feel myself getting better
before.target: bainim taitneamh as labhairt a chleachtadh leat agus tá mé ag baint taitnimh as dul níos fearr

problem: Meaning: the target omits 'more and more' and 'I can feel myself getting better' and says 'I am enjoying going better'.
evidence: 'tá mé ag baint taitnimh as dul níos fearr' does not say what the known says.

before.known: I was hoping to practise speaking with you today
before.target: bhí mé ag súil labhairt a chleachtadh leat inniu

problem: Grammar: 'bhí mé ag súil labhairt' is missing the preposition 'le' (ag súil le ... a dhéanamh).
evidence: 'ag súil le' is the form listed in the course LEGOs; here it is bare.

before.known: I didn't want to ask you but I had no other choice and I can see you do understand
before.target: Ní raibh mé ag iarraidh ceist a chur ort ach ní raibh rogha eile agam agus an dtuigeann tú sin

problem: Meaning: the target says 'and do you understand that' instead of 'I can see you do understand'.
evidence: 'agus an dtuigeann tú sin' is a question, while the known is a statement.

before.known: I didn't want to ask you because she had been trying to find the answer herself
before.target: Ní raibh mé ag iarraidh ceist a chur ort ach go raibh sí ag iarraidh an freagra a fháil di féin

problem: Grammar/meaning: 'ach go raibh sí ... di féin' mistranslates 'because she had been trying'.
evidence: The known says 'because'. The target uses 'ach go' (but that), which changes the meaning.

before.known: I didn't want to ask you again after I had already asked you last week
before.target: Ní raibh mé ag iarraidh ceist a chur ort arís tar éis go raibh mé tar éis ceist a chur ort an tseachtain seo caite

problem: Grammar: 'tar éis go raibh mé tar éis' is ungrammatical and doubles 'tar éis'.
evidence: The known says 'after I had already asked you'.

before.known: I am sorry I didn't want to ask you but I really had no idea what to do next
before.target: Tá brón orm ach Ní raibh mé ag iarraidh ceist a chur ort mar ní raibh a fhios agam cad a bhí le déanamh ansin

problem: Meaning/grammar: the target adds 'mar ní raibh a fhios agam' and a capitalised mid-sentence 'Ní', and the known has no 'because'.
evidence: The known is 'I am sorry I didn't want to ask you but I really had no idea what to do next'. The target is a different sentence.

before.known: I didn't want to ask you at all but I had no other choice and what I needed was only with you
before.target: Ní raibh mé ag iarraidh ceist a chur ort ar chor ar bith ach ní raibh rogha eile agam agus ní raibh cad a bhí de dhíth orm ach agat

problem: Grammar/meaning: 'ní raibh cad a bhí de dhíth orm ach agat' is nonsense Irish and does not match the known.
evidence: The known says 'what I needed was only with you'.

before.known: I think the best option is to keep practising speaking with you until you know how to say it
before.target: ceapaim gur an rogha is fearr ná labhairt a chleachtadh leat go dtí go mbeidh a fhios agat conas é a rá

problem: Grammar: 'gur an rogha is fearr ná' is ungrammatical (gur before an, with a copula missing).
evidence: The known is 'I think the best option is to keep practising speaking with you until ...'.

before.known: I asked if someone could show me how to say it in Irish and they were not sure either
before.target: chuirim ceist an raibh duine éigin ábalta conas é a rá i nGaeilge a thaispeáint dom agus ní raibh siad cinnte

problem: Grammar: 'chuirim ceist an raibh' is present tense and ungrammatical, while the known is past 'I asked'.
evidence: The known says 'I asked if someone could show me ...'.

before.known: I think I am starting to understand how to say it after all the practice we have done together
before.target: ceapaim go bhfuil mé ag tosú ag tuiscint conas é a rá tar éis an méid le chéile

problem: Grammar/meaning: 'tar éis an méid le chéile' is garbled and drops 'practice we have done'.
evidence: The known says 'after all the practice we have done together'.

before.known: I know it can be hard to know how to say it but if you keep going you will get there in the end
before.target: tá a fhios agam go bhfuil sé deacair conas é a rá a fháil amach ach caithfidh tú leanúint ar aghaidh

problem: Meaning: the target 'conas é a rá a fháil amach' garbles the known 'it can be hard to know how to say it', and the second half 'if you keep going you will get there' is missing.
evidence: The Irish ends at 'caithfidh tú leanúint ar aghaidh', so it does not translate the known.

before.known: nobody was sure what was going on and we were all finding it very difficult to know what to say
before.target: Ní raibh duine ar bith cinnte cad a bhí ag tarlú agus bhí sé an-deacair ar gach duine againn a fhios a bheith agat cad a bhí le rá

problem: Grammar: 'a fhios a bheith agat' (you) is used for 'we were all finding it difficult to know'. Agreement is wrong, since it should be 'againn'.
evidence: The known says 'we were all ... to know what to say'.

before.known: I had forgotten how to answer the question and I needed someone to help me remember what to do
before.target: Ní raibh a fhios agam conas an cheist a fhreagairt agus bhí duine de dhíth orm le cabhrú liom cuimhneamh ar cad a bhí le déanamh

problem: Meaning: 'Ní raibh a fhios agam' means 'I didn't know', not 'I had forgotten'.
evidence: S0205 teaches 'tá dearmad déanta agam' for 'I have forgotten'.

before.known: it's important what you needed to do
before.target: Tá sé tábhachtach an méid a bhí le déanamh agat

problem: R8: 'it's important what you needed to do' is not natural English (tier 2 or 3) for a USE row.
evidence: This is an ungrammatical sentence for a USE row and the target mirrors it.

before.known: they want to understand what we are doing but nobody has been able to explain it yet
before.target: Tá siad ag iarraidh a fháil amach cad atá muid a dhéanamh ach ní raibh duine ar bith ábalta é a mhíniú fós

problem: Grammar: 'cad atá muid a dhéanamh' is ungrammatical (it should be 'ag déanamh').
evidence: The known is 'what we are doing'.

before.known: I saw my daughter in the office a while ago
before.target: chonaic mé mo iníon san oifig tamall ó shin

after.target: chonaic mé m'iníon san oifig tamall ó shin

problem: Grammar: 'mo' must elide to 'm'' before a vowel, so 'mo iníon' is wrong.
evidence: The course uses m'eochracha and m'ainm for the same elision.
